# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

items.t: Open connect.punjab.gov.in, find Old Age Pension Scheme in the services list and tap Click to apply service. If you cannot go online, call 1076 and an operator will come home, or visit a Sewa Kendra.
Log in or register with your mobile number and OTP, and complete Aadhaar e-KYC for the person applying.
Fill in the form, upload the age proof, passbook page, self-declaration and the land or property report, and submit. There is no fee.
Note the application number on the receipt and follow it under Track on Connect Punjab.
The CDPO verifies your details and the District Social Security Officer sanctions the pension. The service time is 32 days online and 34 days at a Sewa Kendra.
After sanction, Rs 1,500 a month is credited to your bank account. For problems, contact the District Social Security Officer.
1100 (Connect Punjab and Sewa Kendra helpline) / 1076 (doorstep service) / 0172-2608746 (Social Security head office) / 14567 (elderly helpline)
Lado Protsahan Yojana (Lado Sankalp Patra)
Directorate of Women Empowerment, Women & Child Development Department, Government of Rajasthan

A girl born in a government hospital or a JSY-approved private hospital in Rajasthan is promised Rs 1.5 lakh, paid in seven instalments from birth until she graduates at 21. The scheme began on 1 August 2024, replaced the old Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana (Rajshri girls get their remaining instalments under Lado), and was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.5 lakh in 2025. There is no form: the hospital, the school and the college record her details, and every instalment goes by DBT.
Rs 1,50,000 in 7 instalments — Rs 2,500 at birth up to Rs 1 lakh at graduation
The mother is a resident of Rajasthan and has an Aadhaar card and a Jan Aadhaar card
The girl is born in a government hospital or in a private hospital approved under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
The guidelines set no income or caste condition, and no limit on the number of children for the 3rd instalment onwards
Instalments 3 to 6 need admission in a government school or a state-recognised private school
The last instalment needs graduation from a recognised institution and age 21 completed
A mother living in Rajasthan who delivered outside the state and got JSY can claim the first instalment at her local government hospital

Mukhyamantri Matritva Poshan Yojana (MMMPY)
Directorate of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Women & Child Development Department, Government of Rajasthan

Gives Rs 6,000 in three instalments to a woman pregnant with her second child, for better food and care. It was earlier called the Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana; only the name changed and the rules are the same. If the second baby is a boy, the third instalment is Rs 4,000; if it is a girl, she gets Rs 6,000 under the central PM Matru Vandana Yojana instead, making Rs 8,000 in all. There is no form: the Anganwadi worker or ANM records the pregnancy on PCTS and the money comes by DBT.

Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (Rajasthan top-up to PM-Kisan)
Agriculture Department, Government of Rajasthan

Rajasthan adds its own money to PM-Kisan. Every Rajasthan farmer family that receives PM-Kisan also gets Rs 3,000 a year from the state, paid in instalments of Rs 1,000, so the total becomes Rs 9,000 a year with the Centre's Rs 6,000. There is no separate state form: a farmer registered and active in PM-Kisan gets the state money by DBT automatically.

Nirman Shramik Panjiyan — BOCW Welfare Board (Shramik Card)
Rajasthan Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, Government of Rajasthan

Registers a construction worker with the state welfare board and gives a beneficiary identity card, the shramik card. With it the worker and family can claim the board's schemes: Rs 55,000 under Shubhshakti for a woman worker or an adult unmarried daughter, Rs 21,000 maternity help for a girl and Rs 20,000 for a boy, scholarships for children, up to Rs 1.5 lakh towards a house, and Rs 5 lakh if the worker dies in an accident. Registration is online through SSO and the Labour Department's LDMS, by the worker or at an e-Mitra kiosk.

Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana (MAA Card)
Medical, Health & Family Welfare Department — Rajasthan State Health Assurance Agency (RSHAA), Government of Rajasthan

NFSA and SECC families, small and marginal farmers and government contract workers are covered free; any other family that is not a government employee or pensioner can join by paying Rs 850 a year.

Palanhar Yojana (support for orphan and needy children)
Social Justice & Empowerment Department, Government of Rajasthan

Pays a monthly amount to the relative or guardian (the palanhar) who brings up an orphan, or a child in a listed hardship category, at home, so the child stays with family and keeps studying. Orphans get Rs 1,500 a month up to age 6 and Rs 2,500 from 6 to 18; other categories get Rs 750 and Rs 1,500, and most families also get Rs 2,000 a year for books, clothes and shoes. You apply online at an e-Mitra kiosk, through SSO or on the Palanhar app with face authentication, and renew every July.
